title: Boss: sketch the platform
summary: Model the layers, decide how to onboard a catalogue of APIs, and compute what a design costs.

steps.title: The brief
body: Acme Books is replacing a tangle of point-to-point links with a gateway and an integration layer.
Before anyone writes a route, you are asked to **model** it: the layers as functions, the onboarding
decision for each existing API, and the latency and availability of a proposed call graph.

steps.title: Gateway, integration, backend
prompt: The tests declare `Req`, `Res` and `Handler` as in lesson 2:
```csharp
record Req(string Path, Dictionary<string, string> Headers);
record Res(int Status, string Body);
delegate Res Handler(Req r);
Write two functions:
**`Handler Gateway(Handler next, Dictionary<string, int> quota)`**: `quota` maps each valid token to how many calls it may still make.
- No `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or a token not in `quota` → `Res(401, "unauthorized")`.
- A token whose remaining quota is `0` → `Res(429, "too many requests")`.
- Otherwise decrease that token's quota by one and call `next` with a header copy (case-insensitive) without `Authorization`.
**`Handler Integration(Handler backend)`**: calls `backend` and maps its answer for consumers:
- backend `2xx` → passed through unchanged;
- backend `404` → `Res(404, "not found")`;
- any other backend status → `Res(502, "backend error")` (never pass the backend's own error text on).
starter: Handler Gateway(Handler next, Dictionary<string, int> quota)
solution: Handler Gateway(Handler next, Dictionary<string, int> quota)
if (!quota.TryGetValue(token, out var left)) return new Res(401, "unauthorized");
if (left <= 0) return new Res(429, "too many requests");
var headers = new Dictionary<string, string>(r.Headers, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
hints: Compose them like middleware: the tests call `Gateway(Integration(backend), quota)`.
Check 401 before 429: an unknown token has no quota to look at.
template: Dojo.Eq("missing -> 404 not found", "404 not found", dojo404.Status + " " + dojo404.Body);
Dojo.Eq("backend 500 -> 502 backend error", "502 backend error", dojo502.Status + " " + dojo502.Body);
Dojo.Check("backend never saw Authorization", dojoSaw.All(x => !x.Headers.ContainsKey("Authorization")), "a token reached the backend");
record Req(string Path, Dictionary<string, string> Headers);

steps.title: Onboard the catalogue
prompt: The tests declare:
```csharp
record Api(string Name, bool GenericExecute, bool NeedsBackendSecret, bool CallsSeveralBackends,
bool ProtocolChange, bool HidesFields, bool RenamesFields);
Write `Dictionary<string, List<string>> Plan(List<Api> apis)` that decides each API's shape with the precedence from lesson 3
(`redesign`, `mediation`, `transform`, `pass-through`; there is no validation flag here) and groups the names by shape.
Only shapes that occur appear as keys. Names inside each list are sorted alphabetically (ordinal).
solution: .ToDictionary(g => g.Key, g => g.Select(a => a.Name).OrderBy(n => n, StringComparer.Ordinal).ToList());
hints: A local function `Shape(Api a)` keeps the precedence in one place.
template: new("shipping-rates", false, false, false, false, false, false),
new("catalogue", false, false, false, false, true, true),
new("carrier", false, true, false, false, false, true),
new("billing", false, false, false, true, false, false),
new("reports-execute", true, false, false, false, false, false),
new("authors", false, false, false, false, false, false),
new("order-tracking", false, false, true, false, true, false),
Dojo.Eq("an empty list gives an empty plan", 0, Plan(new List<Api>()).Count);
record Api(string Name, bool GenericExecute, bool NeedsBackendSecret, bool CallsSeveralBackends, bool ProtocolChange, bool HidesFields, bool RenamesFields);

steps.title: What does this design cost?
prompt: An integration calls backends in **stages**: the services inside one stage are called in parallel, and the stages run one after another.
The tests declare `record Call(string Service, double Availability, int LatencyMs);`.
Write `(double Availability, int LatencyMs) Evaluate(List<List<Call>> stages)`:
- availability is the product over **every** call (all must succeed);
- latency is the sum, over stages, of the **slowest** call in that stage. An empty stage adds `0`.
```text
stage 1: catalogue (0.999, 30 ms)
stage 2: warehouse (0.99, 120 ms) + carrier (0.98, 200 ms)   in parallel
solution: foreach (var call in stage) availability *= call.Availability;
hints: Two running totals: multiply availability for every call, add `stage.Max(...)` per stage.
template: var dojoSeq = Evaluate(new List<List<Call>> { new() { new("a", 0.99, 50) }, new() { new("b", 0.99, 50) }, new() { new("c", 0.99, 50) } });
Dojo.Eq("an empty stage costs nothing", (1.0, 0), (dojoEmpty.Availability, dojoEmpty.LatencyMs));
record Call(string Service, double Availability, int LatencyMs);
